application_questions.question: A rectangular tennis court has a perimeter of $72\text{ m}$. Its length is $3\text{ m}$ more than twice its width $w$. Form and solve a linear equation to find the width $w$ and length $l$.

Two kayak hire companies on the Yarra River charge different rates. RiverGlide charges a $\$30$ safety briefing fee plus $\$22$ per hour. PaddleMelb charges a $\$12$ briefing fee plus $\$28$ per hour. For how many hours $h$ of hire are their total charges equal, and what is that charge?
The sum of four consecutive integers is $138$. Let the smallest integer be $n$. Form a linear equation and find all four integers.

An adult ticket to Healesville Sanctuary costs $\$14$ more than a child ticket $c$. A family of $2$ adults and $3$ children pays a total of $\$158$. Form an equation in terms of $c$ and find the price of a child ticket and an adult ticket.

reasoning_questions.question: Find the value of the constant $m$ so that $x = 4$ is the solution to $3(2x - m) = 4x + 2$. Show your substitution and working.
Explain how you can tell without graphing whether the linear equation $4(x - 3) = 2(2x - 6)$ has one solution, no solution, or infinitely many solutions.
reasoning_questions.answer: Infinitely many solutions, because expanding both sides gives the identity $4x - 12 = 4x - 12$, which is true for every real number $x$.

application_questions.question: A hot-water urn at a community footy club starts at $20^\circ\text{C}$ and heats up at a constant rate of $8^\circ\text{C}$ per minute. (a) Write a linear rule for the temperature $T\text{ ($^\circ$C)}$ after $t$ minutes. (b) How many minutes does it take to reach boiling point ($100^\circ\text{C}$)?

A prepaid mobile data pack starts with $45\text{ GB}$ of data and uses $1.5\text{ GB}$ per day. (a) Write a rule for the remaining data $D\text{ (GB)}$ after $t$ days. (b) How much data remains after $18$ days? (c) After how many days is the data completely used up?

A delivery van leaves Bendigo ($150\text{ km}$ from Melbourne) and drives towards Melbourne at a constant speed of $75\text{ km/h}$. Write a linear rule for its distance $d\text{ (km)}$ from Melbourne after $t$ hours, and state the $d$-intercept and $t$-intercept with their physical meanings.
application_questions.answer: $d = -75t + 150$; $d$-intercept $(0, 150)$ is starting distance ($150\text{ km}$); $t$-intercept $(2, 0)$ is arrival time ($2\text{ hours}$).

application_questions.question: A straight line has equation $2x + 3y = 18$. Find its $x$- and $y$-intercepts and calculate the area of the right-angled triangle enclosed by the line and the two coordinate axes.

reasoning_questions.question: Two lines have equations $y = 3x - 4$ and $y = 3x + 5$. Explain using their gradients and $y$-intercepts why these two lines are parallel and never intersect.
reasoning_questions.answer: Both lines have the exact same gradient ($m = 3$), so they rise at the same rate, but they have different $y$-intercepts ($-4 \neq 5$), so they stay $9$ vertical units apart everywhere.

reasoning_questions.question: Determine whether the three points $P(-1, -5)$, $Q(2, 4)$, and $R(6, 16)$ lie on the same straight line (are collinear) by comparing the gradient of $PQ$ with the gradient of $QR$.
reasoning_questions.answer: Yes, they are collinear because $m_{PQ} = \dfrac{4 - (-5)}{2 - (-1)} = 3$ and $m_{QR} = \dfrac{16 - 4}{6 - 2} = 3$.
